expected_failure_regimes: Higher-volatility/liquidity-stress or sparse-observation conditions may create the score without temporary overreaction.
The raw score may have different meaning in persistent-information episodes than in temporary-pressure episodes.
Long recovery and stale carried valuations can make apparent numeric completeness economically fragile.
failure_patterns: Positive local-IS IC and a positive long tail did not clear after-cost long-only risk-adjusted quality; cost, recovery, mechanism, style increment, and capacity remain decisive gaps.
modification_hypotheses: Only after the main-agent memo and human approval: test whether the source-fixed PF/VV score contains residual reversal-related information beyond predeclared PIT industry/log-market-cap controls, while separately keeping a new signed-pressure model as a distinct explore identity. Neither test is authorized or executed by this memo.

Exploit candidate: preserve source PF/VV kernels, fixed negative equal weights, month-end/next-session VWAP timing, and all execution rules; add only a preregistered PIT residual/control measurement and evaluate its information delta versus the immutable parent.

Explore candidate: create a new factor identity with a signed state/observation equation, legal-time definition, explicit retained/deleted-information audit, and permanent-information plus volatility/liquidity nulls; do not alter or relabel the PF/VV parent.
No portfolio-only modification, raw-minute re-scan, OOS access, sign flip, or child execution is permitted.
Human-approved single exploit child only: fixed PF/VV baseline plus a preregistered PIT style-control/residual diagnostic, if data authority permits.
Human-approved new-hypothesis child only: signed-pressure measurement with explicit state, retained/deleted-information audit, permanent-information rival, and volatility/liquidity null.
return_source_hypothesis: The report proposes that unstable conditional excess momentum (PF) and heterogeneous volume-delimited episode returns (VV) reflect short-lived overreaction. If that conjecture is true, lower detector instability should rank better future returns. I retain a mixed behavioral/market-friction hypothesis, not an established risk premium: the same measured close/open/vol paths could reflect permanent information or ordinary low-volatility/liquidity/size exposures. Positive IC is a test of the fixed ranking prediction, not evidence selecting the economic story from these rivals.
reusable_heuristics: Classify finite-mask checks and execution sanity as diagnostic evidence only; retain them for audit but never elevate them into component, payer, or promotion proof.
For source reconstructions with undefined details, retain the baseline convention and record sensitivities rather than choose a formulation from return outcomes.

formula_components.mechanism_requirement: Lower PF is preferred. The daily sum retains selected excess movement; the outer SD deletes daily level/direction. The skew>0 gate itself is asymmetric, so the complete PF construction is not globally sign-invariant.
formula_components.state_interpretation: Conditional same-sign excess momentum variability under the author's right-skewed cross-section gate; not the number of bullish traders.

formula_components.mechanism_requirement: Lower VV is preferred. Volume peaks define boundaries, not volume participation ratios. Unequal segment lengths and sparse prices can mimic this variability; CS normalization before TS SD cannot be commuted.
formula_components.state_interpretation: Author-hypothesized heterogeneous episode price impacts observed through volume-peak partitions; no emotion labels are observed.

formula_components.mechanism_requirement: A fixed source-family ranking, not a sufficient statistic for latent mispricing. Equal weighting discards the PF/VV vector and does not establish a nonlinear interaction or causal component contribution.
formula_components.state_interpretation: Joint relative stability of the two report detectors on a common finite cross-section.

reusable_operator.observation_mapping: Completed-day returns and volume -> same-sign deviation/skew gate daily PF accumulator and volume-peak partition return SD daily VV -> daily VV cross-sectional z-score -> full-calendar 20-day SD -> common-universe component z-scores -> negative equal-weight score.

reuse_constraints: Only reuse as same-factor evidence when artifact_identity matches.
Use as similar-case analogy when factor/report/branch/run identity differs.
success_patterns: The frozen PF/VV source baseline, unlike EVENT_U, has now been reconstructed and has positive local-IS ordering with a positive after-cost G10.
